topic: System design for Read heavy workloads
narration: Say a thousand people want user four two. First request checks a RED-iss cache. It's empty, so it reads from a read replica, not the main database. Then it saves that profile in cache for sixty seconds. The next nine hundred ninety nine requests hit that cache and never touch any database. When someone updates the profile, you delete that cache key. Next read reloads it fresh. Reads scale out. Writes stay safe.
description: Vertical 1080x1920 remotion 2D top-down network diagram on black background, all action in 15-72% height. Top row: cloud of small fg white user dots at 20% height labeled '1000 users want user 42'. Middle: large rounded cache box at 40% height labeled REDIS CACHE in accent cyan, initially empty outline in muted grey. Lower: two cylinders side-by-side at 62% height - left read replica cylinder in accent cyan labeled READ REPLICA, right main database cylinder in muted grey labeled MAIN DB crossed out. Green good bounce-offs, accent3 yellow timer, single accent2 magenta update arrow.
